intended_object: A named proof obligation (a Prop) inside the library's reduction of the genus-five case of the Atanasov–Ranganathan Brill–Noether existence theorem for graphs. It says that every positive subdivision of the loopless split of each valid "pseudocore" with at most eight base vertices carries a divisor of degree 4 and rank at least 1. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `genusFiveRankOneExistence_of_pseudocorePencils`.
explanation: The definition is not a mathematical object in the usual sense. It is an intermediate statement in the library's proof architecture, and it is phrased in terms of the library's own certificate data structures: `Certificate.GenusFourPseudocore.Pseudocore`, `SplitMetadata`, `ValidAt`, `PseudocoreSplitGlue.Compatible` and `Spec`. The docstring says this outright: it is the "finite geometric genus-five boundary produced by the public pseudocore normal form", meant to be discharged later by a catalog theorem or by structural proofs. Its only role is to be fed into `genusFiveRankOneExistence_of_pseudocorePencils`, which derives the real statement from it: every connected genus-5 graph has a g^1_4. The bound `vertexCount ≤ 8` and the split and compatibility conditions are artifacts of the normal-form reduction, not part of any notion in the literature. Mathlib has no counterpart, and comparing it to a textbook definition would not be meaningful. So it is an auxiliary proof device rather than a formalization of a standard object.
